stem: Which expression, written with $\sum$, equals ${=a + b} + {=2*a + b} + {=3*a + b} + \dots + ({=a}\times {=n} + {=b})$, whose general term is $({=a}r + {=b})$ for $r = 1, 2, 3, \dots, {=n}$?
solution: Terms are ${=a}\times 1 + {=b}$, ${=a}\times 2 + {=b}$, ... so the general term is ${=a}r + {=b}$.
The first term has $r = 1$ and the last has $r = {=n}$.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Wrong limits
proposed_misconceptions.description: Starts the index at 0 and stops at n-1, which changes the terms.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Wrong general term
proposed_misconceptions.description: Writes a general term that does not reproduce the terms given, by factoring or grouping wrongly.

notes: No book questions supplied; parent is placeholder. Standard: write a sum using sigma.
